title: Wedding Guest Dress Colors to Avoid
metaTitle: Wedding Guest Dress Colors to Avoid: White, Red & Culture
metaDescription: Wedding guest dress colors to avoid: white and near-whites first, then the bridesmaids' color and cultural rules for Chinese, Indian and Vietnamese weddings.
h1: Wedding Guest Dress Colors to Avoid, Shade by Shade and Culture by Culture
answer: Avoid white and anything that reads as white: ivory, cream, champagne, beige, off-white and prints on a white base, unless the couple asks for it. Then check three things: the bridesmaids' color, any palette on the invitation, and the couple's tradition (red is a bridal color in Chinese, Indian and Vietnamese weddings; white is the Chinese mourning color). Black, red, gold and prints are fine at most Western weddings. Men: a white shirt is fine, a white suit is not.
intro: Wedding guest dress colors to avoid come down to one firm rule and a few situational checks. The firm rule is white, including every shade a camera can mistake for white. The checks are the wedding party's color, the couple's published palette, and the colors that carry a meaning in the couple's tradition. Almost everything else on the old lists of banned colors, black and red included, is folklore at a modern Western wedding. This guide gives a verdict for each color, shows which near-white shades real guests worry about most, sets out the cultural rules we could source, and covers men's shirts, suits and dinner jackets as well as dresses.

contentSections.heading: Rule one: don't wear white, and know what counts as white
contentSections.content:
Every source read for this page agrees on white. Etiquette expert Elaine Swann told TODAY in January 2026: "Any shades of white, that color is still reserved for the bride. However, white is acceptable when the bride and groom ask you to wear it." Bridal stylist Anny Choi gave Vogue the same answer: "The simple answer is 'no,' unless the invite calls for it," and told Vogue the rule also covers cream, ivory and beige.

The reason is simple. Brides in Western weddings have worn white since Queen Victoria's 1840 wedding made it fashionable, according to Wikipedia's articles on the white wedding and the wedding dress, and a guest in the same color competes with her in every photograph. The rule also applies when both partners are grooms; Vogue notes it is still a color held by the couple.

So can you wear white to a wedding? Only when invited to. Some couples throw an all-white party or ask for white at a welcome event; in that case Choi advises a solid white rather than a white floral, because a floral is likely what the bride will wear. Everywhere else, the shades to skip are white, ivory, cream, beige, off-white and champagne, together with any outfit where one of those is the dominant color.

contentSections.heading: Test the near-whites in daylight before you commit
contentSections.content:
The hardest cases are colors that look obviously colored on a hanger and pale under a flash. Choi warns Vogue readers that a pale pink or butter yellow can be "a tad too close to a cream hue" in photographs. Stylist Micaela Erlanger gives the workable rule: "As long as the main color doesn't read as white, you're in the clear." Vogue adds a print rule: if the base of the dress is white and the print is another color, avoid it; a colorful dress with white in the print is probably fine.

Real guests struggle with exactly these shades. In our analysis of 10,700 posts on r/Weddingattireapproval (16 April – 21 October 2026), 944 carry the subreddit's "Is this too white?" flair. We searched their titles and text for each shade or pattern word. 742 of them (78.6%) use the word white, but 202 (21.4%) never do, because the outfit in question is cream, yellow, a pastel or a print. Cream leads the named shades with 81 posts, then yellow with 70; floral or other prints appear in 145 posts (15.4%), and 24 describe a white background or base.

The check that settles most of them: photograph the outfit outdoors in daylight and again indoors with the flash on. If either photo looks white or cream, choose something else, or add enough color (a jacket, a wrap, a bold shoe and bag) that the overall impression stops reading as bridal.

contentSections.heading: Ignore the myths: black, red and gold are usually fine
contentSections.content:
Many lists of wedding guest dress colors to avoid pad themselves with colors that etiquette writers no longer object to.

Black. Vogue contributor Alexandra Macon calls black at a wedding "perfectly acceptable, and chic" as long as it is festive and not funereal, and the Emily Post Institute's attire guide lists a little black dress under black tie, black tie optional and semi-formal. The caution applies at some cultural weddings, covered below, and in the details of the full guide to wearing black.

Red. Swann calls the no-red rule "another internet fable" in the U.S., while Diane Gottsman, quoted by Who What Wear, draws the line at a loud, crowd-stopping red. A deep or patterned red is fine at most Western weddings.

Gold, silver and metallics. Nothing in the Emily Post lists restricts them, and they suit evening and black tie weddings. The one caution is pale gold or rose gold so light that it looks like champagne, which takes it back to the near-white problem.

Navy, jewel tones, prints and saturated pastels are all safe defaults. If an outfit is obviously a color, not white, and not the bridesmaids' color, you are almost always fine.

contentSections.heading: Find out the bridesmaids' color before you buy
contentSections.content:
The second most common color mistake is not offensive, just awkward: turning up in the exact shade and length the bridesmaids are wearing, and appearing to belong to the wedding party in every group photograph.

In our Reddit analysis, 101 posts explicitly state what the bridesmaids are wearing (phrases like "bridesmaids are wearing" or "bridesmaids will be in"), which shows how often guests plan around it. Cosmopolitan UK's guide to black makes the same suggestion: the invitation usually hints at the wedding's colors, and you can ask the couple which colors to avoid.

How to find out: check the wedding website, look at the save-the-date and invitation colors, and if it is still unclear, ask a member of the wedding party. If you already own a dress in the wedding party's color, change something visible: a different length, a print rather than a solid, or a contrasting jacket or wrap. Men have the same issue with ties: if the groomsmen wear a particular colored tie, pick a different one.

contentSections.heading: Colors that carry meaning in other wedding traditions
contentSections.content:
The colors to avoid change at weddings that follow a non-Western tradition, and these are the rules most likely to matter because getting them wrong can genuinely offend. Below is what we could verify from named sources. Where a source does not cover a tradition, the table says so rather than guessing.

Chinese weddings. Red is a traditional bridal color: Wikipedia's article on Chinese marriage says modern brides generally pick red, following tradition, or white. White is the traditional mourning color, according to Wikipedia's articles on color in Chinese culture and on mourning, and the same Chinese color article says black has less mourning association than white. Swann says red is highly inappropriate for guests at Chinese and Indian weddings.

Indian weddings. Wikipedia's wedding sari article says wedding saris are usually red, a color associated with married women, with variation by region, caste and religion. Vogue and Swann both advise guests not to wear red. Cosmopolitan UK adds that black is still associated with mourning at traditional Indian and Chinese weddings, a claim the Wikipedia articles read for this page do not make for India, so the safe move is a saturated color that is neither red, black nor white.

Vietnamese weddings. Wikipedia's traditional Vietnamese wedding article says reds and pinks remain popular for brides, that brides may also wear a Western white gown, and that guests wear their own áo dài or formal Western clothes.

Japanese weddings. Wikipedia says Japanese brides may wear a white shiromuku kimono, and that at Japanese funerals all guests wear black, with men in black suits, white shirts and black ties. Avoid white, and men should avoid pairing a black suit with a black tie.

Korean and Mexican weddings. Wikipedia's article on marriage in Korea says many couples hold a Westernized ceremony with a tuxedo and white gown before a smaller traditional one; it gives no guest color rule. We found no named, fetchable source for a Mexican wedding guest color rule. At both, follow the general rules above and ask the couple about anything specific.

contentSections.heading: Men's colors: the white shirt is fine, the white suit is not
contentSections.content:
The color rules apply to men, with a different set of garments. Vogue's white guide says men should abstain from a white jacket or white trousers, while a white button-down shirt is allowed and often encouraged. That matches every dress code in the Emily Post Institute's attire guide, which puts a white shirt at the center of black tie and black tie optional.

The one white jacket the etiquette rules allow is the white dinner jacket. Emily Post lists it for black tie in summer, in the tropics or on a cruise, worn with black tuxedo trousers. At a summer black tie wedding it is correct, but check that the groom is not wearing one before you choose it.

Other men's checks:

• Ties and pocket squares: avoid the groomsmen's exact color; red accents are fine at most Western weddings and worth a question at Chinese, Indian or Vietnamese weddings.
• All black: a black suit with a white shirt is fine; a black suit, black shirt and black tie together reads as funeral dress, and at a Japanese wedding a black tie with a black suit is the funeral combination.
• Light suits: tan, light grey and pale blue suits are normal at daytime and summer weddings; a cream or ivory suit is not.

contentSections.heading: Sequins, sparkle and statement prints
contentSections.content:
Sparkle is a formality question more than a color one. Fabric that catches light reads as evening, which makes all-over sequins and beading natural at a black tie or evening formal wedding and heavy at a noon garden ceremony. Erlanger's advice to Vogue readers is to avoid colors that really stand out, neons included, unless the party clearly calls for it.

Two combinations to skip anywhere: sequins or beading in ivory, champagne or silver-white, which look bridal, and lace in white or cream, which Vogue singles out as reading "quite bridal." Bold prints are fine as long as the dominant color is not white and the print is not on a white base.

contentSections.heading: Already bought something that might be too close? Here's what to do
contentSections.content:
If you are reading this with a dress already in the closet, you have four options, roughly in order of effort.

• Ask. Send the couple or a member of the wedding party a photo in daylight and ask honestly. If they say it is fine, it is fine.
• Add color. A colored jacket, blazer or wrap kept on through the ceremony and photos, plus a saturated shoe and bag, changes the overall read of a pale dress.
• Save it. A cream or champagne dress that is wrong for a wedding is often right for another event, so you lose nothing by keeping it for later.
• Swap. If the answer is still unclear a week before, choose something that is obviously a color. Navy and emerald never raise a color question.

faqs.question: Can you wear white shoes to a wedding?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, when the rest of the outfit is clearly colored. The rule targets an overall white look; Erlanger's test is whether the main color reads as white. White shoes with a white or cream dress, or white accessories that add up to a mostly white outfit, should be avoided. For men, Emily Post lists sneakers only under casual, so white sneakers belong at casual weddings.

faqs.question: Can you wear a white floral dress to a wedding?
faqs.answer: Not if the background is white. Vogue's rule is that a white base with a colored print should be avoided, while a colorful dress with some white in the print is probably fine. In our Reddit analysis, 145 of the 944 "Is this too white?" posts concern floral or other prints, so it is one of the most common gray areas.

faqs.question: What colors should you not wear to an Indian or Chinese wedding?
faqs.answer: Avoid red, which is a traditional bridal color in both. At a Chinese wedding also avoid white, the traditional mourning color. For Indian weddings, sources disagree on black and white, and wedding colors vary by region and religion, so choose a saturated color that is none of the three, or ask the family.
